safety_observation.name: safety_observation
safety_observation.description: A safety observation refers to any recorded note or report about workplace conditions, behaviors, or practices that may impact health and safety. These observations are typically made by workers, supervisors, or safety personnel during routine checks or daily activities, and can include both positive and negative findings related to safety compliance or risks.
examples: Observed all workers wearing required PPE in the welding area.
Noted that emergency exits were clear and unobstructed.
Identified a missing guard on the conveyor belt during inspection.
Observed forklift operator following safe driving procedures.
Noticed a spill in the loading dock that was not yet cleaned up.

near_miss.name: near_miss
near_miss.description: A near miss is an unplanned event that did not result in injury, illness, or damage but had the potential to do so. In HSE, near misses are reported to identify hazards and prevent future incidents by addressing underlying causes before harm occurs.
examples: A falling tool landed next to a worker but caused no injury.
Forklift narrowly missed striking a pallet left in the aisle.
Employee slipped on wet floor but regained balance without falling.
Overhead load swung out of control but did not hit anyone.
Chemical container was dropped but did not break or spill.

incident.name: incident
incident.description: An incident is any unplanned event that results in or could have resulted in injury, illness, property damage, or environmental harm. In HSE, incidents are formally reported and investigated to determine root causes and prevent recurrence.
examples: Worker sustained a laceration while using a box cutter.
Forklift collided with a storage rack causing minor damage.
Employee suffered a sprained ankle after tripping on uneven flooring.
Oil spill occurred during equipment maintenance.
Fire alarm triggered due to electrical short circuit.

hazard_report.name: hazard_report
hazard_report.description: A hazard report documents the identification of a condition, process, or behavior that poses a risk to health, safety, or the environment. These reports are used to alert management and prompt corrective actions before an incident occurs.
examples: Reported exposed wiring near the main switchboard.
Identified unguarded machinery in the production area.
Noted chemical storage containers without proper labeling.
Reported blocked emergency eyewash station.
Observed trip hazard due to loose floor tiles.

environmental_observation.name: environmental_observation
environmental_observation.description: An environmental observation records any condition or event that may impact the environment, such as pollution, waste, or resource misuse. In HSE, these observations help organizations monitor compliance with environmental standards and identify areas for improvement.
examples: Observed oil sheen on surface water near the facility.
Noted improper disposal of chemical waste in the dumpster.
Identified excessive dust emissions from the crusher.
Reported leaking valve causing water runoff.
Observed wildlife entering the waste storage area.

quality_issue.name: quality_issue
quality_issue.description: A quality issue refers to any deviation from established standards or specifications that could affect product integrity, safety, or compliance. In HSE, quality issues are reported when they have potential safety, health, or environmental implications.
examples: Found welds not meeting required strength specifications.
Identified mislabeled chemical containers in storage.
Detected faulty emergency stop button on machinery.
Observed packaging not sealing properly on finished goods.
Reported incorrect calibration of gas detection equipment.

maintenance_request.name: maintenance_request
maintenance_request.description: A maintenance request is a formal notification to repair, replace, or service equipment, infrastructure, or safety systems. In HSE, timely maintenance requests help prevent equipment failures that could lead to safety incidents or environmental harm.
examples: Requested repair of faulty emergency lighting in stairwell.
Submitted work order for leaking compressed air line.
Reported malfunctioning fire alarm panel for service.
Requested replacement of worn-out machine guard.
Notified maintenance about broken eyewash station.

unsafe_condition.name: unsafe_condition
unsafe_condition.description: An unsafe condition is any physical state or environmental factor in the workplace that increases the risk of injury, illness, or damage. Reporting unsafe conditions is critical in HSE to prompt corrective actions and prevent incidents.
examples: Found wet floor without warning signs in hallway.
Observed missing handrail on stairway.
Noted poor lighting in storage area.
Identified unguarded rotating equipment.
Reported blocked fire exit door.

unsafe_act.name: unsafe_act
unsafe_act.description: An unsafe act is any behavior or action by a person that increases the likelihood of an accident or injury. In HSE, unsafe acts are reported to address risky behaviors and reinforce safe work practices.
examples: Worker bypassed machine guard to speed up process.
Employee climbed shelving to retrieve item instead of using ladder.
Observed forklift operator using mobile phone while driving.
Worker entered confined space without proper permit.
Employee failed to wear required hearing protection in noisy area.
